Build PHASE 3 of the Nxeon "Cold Email Engine" — the deliverability/scale layer the owner asked for (warming, real analytics, multiple domains/inboxes). Work ONLY in the ISOLATED worktree /opt/nxeon-build-ce (branch feature/coldemail-phase3, off main 7f7a758 which already has CE Phase 1+2).

=== ABSOLUTE ISOLATION (a prior run broke prod by ignoring this) ===
- Do ALL work in /opt/nxeon-build-ce. NEVER touch /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging (no cd, no build, no writes, no git ops there).
- First: `cd /opt/nxeon-build-ce && npm ci` for this worktree's OWN node_modules (do NOT symlink/reuse another tree's). Run `npx prisma generate`/`npm run build` ONLY here.
- NEVER systemctl, restart, deploy, `prisma db push` any DB, or edit .env. Verify `pwd` is under /opt/nxeon-build-ce and branch is feature/coldemail-phase3 before building.

=== READ FIRST ===
- The current-2026 research + concrete Phase 3 spec: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/coldemail/phase3-research.md (follow its build spec).
- Existing CE code you're extending: prisma/schema.prisma (models Business/Contact/Brand/EmailList/Suppression/ConsentRecord/ColdCampaign/SequenceStep/ColdSend/EmailEvent + enums), lib/coldemail/{compliance,sender,feedback}.ts, worker/coldemail.ts, lib/actions-coldemail.ts, app/admin/coldemail/* and its nav under the "Cold Email" entry. Reuse components/ui/primitives.tsx.

=== HARD PRODUCT GUARDRAILS ===
- Master send switch `cold_email_sending_enabled` stays OFF by default; NOTHING sends. Keep reputation-isolation (no sending from nxeon.cloud/protected domains) and all Phase 1/2 compliance intact.
- Analytics must be HONEST about open tracking: per the research, Apple Mail Privacy Protection auto-opens 50%+ of mail, so opens are inflated. Show open rate but clearly label it "unreliable (MPP-inflated) — do not optimize on this"; make reply/positive-reply, bounce, complaint, click, unsubscribe, and inbox-placement the primary health signals.

=== PHASE 3 DELIVERABLES (additive schema; keep names consistent) ===
1) Multi-domain / multi-inbox model: a SendingDomain (domain, subdomain strategy, custom tracking domain, SPF/DKIM/DMARC verified flags, reputation/health, status) and a Mailbox/Inbox (belongs to a SendingDomain + Brand; address, provider, dailyCap, status ACTIVE/WARMING/PAUSED/BURNING, health score, lastSendAt). A Brand can have multiple domains; a domain multiple inboxes.
2) Warming: per-inbox warmup schedule/state (warmupStartedAt, stage, currentDailyLimit ramping ~5→20-40 over ~2-4 weeks), a warmup engine (pure + worker step) that computes today's allowed volume per inbox, and a Warming UI showing each inbox's stage/ramp/health. Favor real-reply/positive-signal warmup per the research; DO NOT build a synthetic warmup-network that sends real mail (flag it as SaaS-pool territory, out of scope). No actual sending.
3) Send rotation: extend worker/coldemail.ts to ROTATE across a campaign brand's eligible inboxes, honoring each inbox's warmup limit + dailyCap, and AUTO-PAUSE an inbox at ~1.8% bounce and a domain at >0.08% complaint (thresholds from the research; make them Settings). Pure, testable rotation + threshold logic.
4) Analytics: deliverability event rollups (daily per inbox / domain / campaign): sent, delivered, hard-bounce, soft-bounce, complaint, click, reply, unsubscribe, and rates derived from them (delivery %, bounce %, complaint %, click %, reply %, unsubscribe %) + an inbox-placement/seed-test hook (structure the model + a manual "record seed result" action; no external API). Dashboards at /admin/coldemail (overview trends) + a per-domain and per-inbox health view. Extend EmailEvent types as needed (REPLY, POSITIVE_REPLY, DELIVERED, HARD_BOUNCE/SOFT_BOUNCE distinction) additively.
5) Compliance surfacing: a readiness panel per domain reflecting the 2026 bulk-sender rules (aligned SPF+DKIM+DMARC, RFC 8058 one-click unsub, <0.3% spam-rate target, custom tracking domain) with red/green; link to the guidance. 
6) Server actions in lib/actions-coldemail.ts (each re-checks requireArea("platform")); nav tabs under the "Cold Email" entry for Domains/Inboxes, Warming, Analytics. Tests for warmup-ramp math, rotation, and auto-pause thresholds. Update docs/DOCUMENTATION.md.

When done: in /opt/nxeon-build-ce, `npx prisma generate` + `npm run build` MUST pass 0 errors; tests pass; commit + `git push` feature/coldemail-phase3. Report: files added/changed, schema additions, the metrics/thresholds implemented, how open-rate is handled, build/test result. Do NOT deploy, do NOT touch prod.

1	# Cold Email Engine — Phase 3 Research & Build Spec
2	
3	Research compiled **2026-08-11**. Cold email is a fast-moving space (ISP rules + regulation change quarterly), so every claim below is dated and cited. Treat anything older than ~12 months as "verify before relying on it."
4	
5	> **TL;DR for the owner:** The single most important 2026 change is that **open rate is no longer a real metric** and **inbox access is now gated by mandatory authentication, not by content**. Apple Mail Privacy Protection (MPP) auto-opens ~50%+ of email, so open rate is inflated noise; meanwhile Google/Yahoo (Feb 2024) and Microsoft (May 2025) will *reject* mail that isn't SPF+DKIM+DMARC authenticated with one-click unsubscribe and a spam-complaint rate under 0.3%. Phase 3 must be built around **reply rate, bounce rate, complaint rate, and inbox-placement** — not opens — and around **health-monitored multi-inbox rotation with auto-pause**, because a single burned domain now poisons all recipients on it.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1) Active open-source platforms (2026)
10	
11	Important framing: there is **no fully-featured OSS clone of Instantly/Smartlead** that includes a real shared warmup network — the network effect (tens of thousands of vetted, engaged mailboxes) is the moat those SaaS products actually sell, and it can't be self-hosted alone. OSS covers the *sending/campaign/MTA* layer well and the *warmup* layer poorly. Categorize as: (A) sending MTAs, (B) campaign/marketing platforms, (C) cold-email/warmup-specific tools.
12	
13	### A. Sending MTAs (the outbound engine)
14	
15	| Tool | What it is | Stack | License | Self-host | Analytics exposed |
16	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
17	| **Postal** | App-oriented mail platform: SMTP send, inbound routing, webhooks, IP pools, multi-tenant orgs, DKIM/SPF/Return-Path. Docker/K8s, OIDC SSO, Prometheus metrics. Actively maintained. | Ruby on Rails, MySQL/MariaDB, RabbitMQ | MIT | Yes | Open (1x1 pixel), click (link rewrite), delivery/bounce via webhooks, Prometheus |
18	| **KumoMTA** | Open-source high-performance MTA (built by ex-PowerMTA team) for high-volume outbound; per-IP/domain shaping, traffic policy, queues. 500K–10M+/mo. | Rust | Apache 2.0 | Yes | Delivery logs, per-domain shaping metrics; pairs with external analytics |
19	| **Mailcow / Mailu / Stalwart** | Full mailbox servers (Postfix/Dovecot etc.), not cold-email tools. Good for *hosting the actual mailboxes/IMAP* an outreach tool sends through. Mailcow = polished SMB UI; Stalwart = low-resource Rust; Mailu = minimal/K8s. | Various | Various (mostly permissive/GPL) | Yes | Server-level, not campaign-level |
20	
21	Sources: [Postal openalternative.co](https://openalternative.co/postal) (2026), [smtpedia Postal guide](https://smtpedia.com/postal-guide/) (2026), [KumoMTA GitHub](https://github.com/KumoCorp/kumomta) (2026), [Mailflow: MTA options compared](https://mailflowauthority.com/email-infrastructure/mta-options-compared) (2026), [profor.pro mailcow vs Stalwart vs Mailu](https://profor.pro/blog/self-hosted-email-2026-mailcow-stalwart-mailu/) (2026).
22	
23	### B. Campaign / email-marketing platforms (broadcast, not cold-outreach-native)
24	
25	| Tool | Stack | License | Notes |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| **listmonk** | Go + Postgres | AGPLv3 | Fast, simple, high-performance lists/campaigns; needs external SMTP relay (SES/Mailgun). Opens/clicks/bounces. |
28	| **Mautic** | PHP/Symfony | GPLv3 | Deepest OSS marketing automation (segmentation, campaign flows, scoring). Heavier. |
29	| **Mailcoach** | Laravel package | Commercial license (self-host) | Not free; polished. |
30	| **Keila** | Elixir/Phoenix | AGPLv3 | Modern UI, EU/privacy-focused, no-code automations. |
31	| **phpList / Mailtrain** | PHP / Node | AGPLv3 / GPLv3 | Older but maintained. |
32	
33	Note the **license split**: AGPLv3 (listmonk, Keila, phpList) triggers a *source-disclosure obligation when offered as a network service* — relevant if Nxeon exposes these to customers as SaaS. GPLv3 (Mautic, Mailtrain) has no network clause; private SaaS modifications stay private. Sources: [sendbroadcast self-hosted email marketing 2026](https://sendbroadcast.net/self-hosted/email-marketing-software), [awwtomation OSS email platforms 2026](https://www.awwtomation.com/blog/best-open-source-email-marketing-platforms), [mailflowauthority OSS newsletter platforms](https://mailflowauthority.com/email-comparisons/open-source-newsletter-platforms).
34	
35	### C. Cold-email / warmup-specific OSS (thin, verify before trusting)
36	
37	- **Warmbly** — the closest thing to an OSS Instantly/Smartlead. "Open-source AI-native cold outreach + email warmup," Apache 2.0, on GitHub, self-hostable *for the sending/inbox/CRM/API stack*. **Key limitation, and it proves the general point:** the shared warmup pool runs on *their* cloud and needs a large base of vetted mailboxes — a single self-hosted instance starts with none. [warmbly.com](https://warmbly.com/), [github.com/warmbly/warmbly](https://github.com/warmbly/warmbly) (2026).
38	- **Outbound Tools** (deploy-template, Railway) — lightweight IMAP/SMTP outbound ops server: campaign sending, reply classification, segmentation, deliverability metrics. Positioned as OSS Lemlist/Instantly/Smartlead alt. [railway.com/deploy/outbound-tools](https://railway.com/deploy/outbound-tools).
39	- Various small GitHub repos (PaulleDemon/Email-automation, meteor-emails, dancolta/trustpilot-outreach-automation) — single-purpose, low-maturity, useful as reference, not production. [github topics: cold-emails](https://github.com/topics/cold-emails).
40	- **Skepticism flag:** blog listicles cite "Mailwarm-OSS" and "InboxAuto" as OSS warmup tools; I could not verify maintained repos for those names and treat them as **unconfirmed / likely SEO filler**. The honest 2026 conclusion: **a legitimate, self-hosted, mature OSS warmup *network* does not exist** — you either build a private engagement loop yourself or rent a network.
41	
42	Sources: [dev.to open-source email warmup guide](https://dev.to/tusharsmtpmaster/open-source-email-warmup-a-complete-guide-5d5b), [github esli351/best-email-tools](https://github.com/esli351/best-email-tools).
43	
44	**Implication for Nxeon:** Phase 3 is not "adopt an OSS platform." It's "keep the existing Next.js/Prisma app as the control plane, send through customers' own IMAP/SMTP mailboxes (or a Postal/KumoMTA relay), and build warmup + analytics + rotation ourselves." Postal is the best OSS reference for the *events/webhooks/tracking* model; KumoMTA is the reference if we ever run our own IPs.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## 2) Email warming — current mechanics (2026)
49	
50	**Why it still exists:** Gmail and Microsoft tightened filtering; brand-new domains/inboxes are flagged immediately. Warmup builds a history of "normal, trusted" sending — gradually rising volume + positive engagement (opens, replies, marking important, rescuing from spam) — so that by the time a real campaign sends, the provider already trusts the sender. ([omnisend warmup 2026](https://www.omnisend.com/blog/warm-up-email-domain/), [reply.io warm-up 2026](https://reply.io/warm-up-email/))
51	
52	**Modern ramp schedule (consensus 2026):**
53	- New inbox starts ~**5–10 emails/day**, ramps to **40–50/day** over **2–4 weeks** (MailReach's default is ~10/day wk1 → 40–50 by wk4). A "fully warmed" inbox tops out around **50–100/day** at **3–5 weeks**. ([mailreach gmail warmup](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/gmail-warmup), [leadhaste timeline](https://leadhaste.com/blog/email-warmup-timeline-and-schedule))
54	- Pre-warmed inboxes can start higher (Smartlead guidance: ~80/day wk1 → 150–180 by day 30). ([litemail smartlead warmup](https://litemail.ai/blog/email-warmup-smartlead-best-tool-2026))
55	- **AI/adaptive ramp** is now standard: Smartlead/MailReach adjust ramp speed in real time off a live "health score" instead of a fixed daily increment. MailReach cites a network of 30,000+ Google Workspace / M365 accounts + a "Co-Pilot" that reads deliverability signals. ([maildeck warmup tools 2026](https://maildeck.co/blog/best-email-warm-up-tools-2026/))
56	
57	**Warmup activities the networks simulate:** send between pool inboxes, auto-open, auto-reply, mark-as-important/star, and **rescue from spam → move to inbox** (the strongest signal). Seed inboxes across Gmail/M365/Yahoo. ([smartlead warm-up guide](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/email-warm-up-guide))
58	
59	**The 2026 debate — does artificial warmup still help, or now hurt?** This is genuinely contested and Phase 3 must be honest about it:
60	- **Against:** most warmup tools generate *artificial* opens/clicks between simulated inboxes — literally trying to manipulate the spam filters whose job is to protect real users. Recent Gmail/Yahoo updates that reward *long-term domain reputation and real authentication* are increasingly good at detecting these synthetic patterns, and **when detected can actively damage deliverability**. The safest posture is warmup that produces *replies and spam-recovery on a vetted pool*, not mass auto-opens.

68	**Isolate the sending domain (universal in 2026).** Never cold-send from the primary brand domain — at volume it now *burns* the primary. Buy separate lookalike domains (e.g. `try-brand.com`, `getbrand.co`) and send from a **subdomain** (`mail.` / `outreach.`) so any reputation damage is quarantined off the root. 72	- **Per-inbox daily cap: 20–40** for a warmed inbox (newer inboxes 10–15), i.e. **~100–250/domain/day** across 3–5 inboxes. Space sends **90–120s apart** across a sending window — 40 rapid sends in an hour reads as bot behavior. ([ozigi caps](https://ozigi.app/blog/how-many-cold-emails-per-day-without-spam))

Only enable open tracking behind a custom domain (and see §4 on why opens barely matter now). ([mailflowauthority infra](https://mailflowauthority.com/cold-email/cold-email-infrastructure-complete-guide))

78	**Content variation / spintax:** the #1 content-level deliverability killer is **duplicate content** — identical bodies to many recipients from one domain get fingerprinted as bulk. Spintax (`{Hi|Hello|Hey}`) makes each send unique. **Nuance:** word-level spintax "barely moves deliverability"; **sentence/paragraph-level variation with 6–10 meaningful variants** is where the lift is. Personalization matters more: emails with ≥2 personalizations get 5.6% reply vs 3.6% with none (Hunter.io 2026 State of Cold Email). ([smartlead spintax](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/what-is-spintax), [mailreach spintax](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/spintax-cold-email))

92	## 4) Analytics that actually matter now
93	
94	**Metric definitions (2026):**
95	- **Delivery rate** = accepted by receiving server ÷ sent. High delivery ≠ inbox; it only means "not bounced/rejected." Do not confuse with placement.
96	- **Inbox-placement rate** = of delivered mail, % landing in the primary inbox (vs spam/Promotions/missing). Measured via seed tests (§3), *not* from your own send logs. **Good ≥90%, best-in-class ≥95%.** ([amplemarket 2026 benchmarks](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks))
97	- **Open rate** = pixel loads ÷ delivered. **Largely broken — see below.**
98	- **Click rate** = unique clickers ÷ delivered. More reliable than opens but distorted by security scanners/link-preview bots that auto-click.
99	- **Bounce rate** = bounces ÷ sent. **Hard bounce** = permanent (bad/nonexistent address) → suppress forever. **Soft bounce** = temporary (mailbox full, greylisting, size).
100	- **Spam-complaint rate** = complaints ÷ delivered (via Postmaster/FBL).
101	- **Unsubscribe rate** = unsubs ÷ delivered.
102	- **Reply rate** and **positive-reply rate** = replies (and positive/interested replies) ÷ delivered. **The KPI that matters most in 2026.**
103	
104	**Open tracking is unreliable — be honest in the UI.** Apple Mail Privacy Protection (since 2021, escalated through iOS 18) **pre-loads all remote content including tracking pixels on Apple's servers**, so emails register as "opened" even when unread. Apple Mail is ~51% of the global email-client market and **>55% of all global opens now come from Apple/MPP devices** — meaning the majority of "opens" are machine-generated. Corporate security scanners (Proofpoint/Mimecast/Defender) also pre-fetch pixels *and* links. **Net: open rate is inflated, non-comparable, and unsafe as an optimization target or a health signal.** ([sender.net MPP 2026 guide](https://www.sender.net/blog/apple-mail-privacy-protection/), [hustlermarketing 3 metrics replacing open rate](https://www.hustlermarketing.com/blog/3-email-metrics-that-are-replacing-open-rate-in-2026/), [instantly open-tracking accuracy](https://instantly.ai/blog/email-open-tracking-how-it-works-accuracy-rates-and-why-your-open-metrics-may-be-wrong/))
105	
106	**What leaders optimize instead (MPP-proof signals):**
107	1. **Reply rate / positive-reply rate** — replies require human intent; mailbox providers treat replies as a strong positive trust signal. This is the primary campaign KPI.
108	2. **Click rate** — MPP-resistant (MPP proxies pixels, not user clicks), though filter clicking distorts it.
109	3. **Complaint rate + bounce rate + unsubscribe rate** — combined into a "disaffection/disengagement" index; the clearest early warning of a burning domain.
110	4. **Inbox-placement rate** from seed tests — the ground truth for "are we even in the inbox."
111	
112	**Benchmarks (2026, deliverability-managed vs raw):**
113	| Metric | Good | Best-in-class | Danger |
114	|---|---|---|---|
115	| Inbox placement | ≥90% | ≥95% | <80% |
116	| Bounce | <3% | <1.5% | >5% → stop & diagnose |
117	| Reply | 1–5% | 8–10%+ | — |
118	| Spam complaint | <0.1% | ~0% | 0.3% hard ceiling |
119	| Open (context only) | 15–25% raw | not a target | ignore |
120	Source: [amplemarket 2026](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks).
121	
122	**"Domain/inbox is burning" thresholds (auto-pause triggers):**
123	- **Bounce:** <2% safe · 2–5% warning (Postmaster reputation degrading, clean list before continuing) · >5% danger (immediate pause + re-verify). Sustained >2% for 5–7 days suppresses inbox placement for *all* Gmail recipients on that domain, not just the bad addresses. **Recommended auto-pause at ~1.8% per inbox/day** (before the ceiling). ([litemail bounce thresholds](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-inbox-bounce-rate-thresholds-2026))
124	- **Complaint:** <0.05% safe · 0.05–0.08% warning · **>0.08% pause the whole domain and investigate targeting** (Google effectively treats ~0.1%+ as a problem; 0.3% is the hard mandate ceiling). Complaint spikes = wrong ICP or deceptive copy. ([amplemarket](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks), [litemail health metrics](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-inbox-health-metrics-2026))

128	## 5) CURRENT regulation + ISP requirements (the fast-changing part) — what's mandatory NOW
129	
130	This is what gates the inbox *at all* in 2026. Non-compliant senders see **22–34% of mail routed to spam vs 89% inbox placement for compliant senders** — a 3–7x penalty. ([mailover 2026 guide](https://mailover.ai/blog/bulk-sender-requirements.html))

132	**Google + Yahoo — "Yahoogle" (announced Oct 2023, enforced Feb 1 2024), for senders of 5,000+/day to consumer Gmail/Yahoo:**
133	- **SPF + DKIM** both configured and passing; **at least one aligned** to the From-header domain.
134	- **DMARC** published, minimum **p=none** with a RUA reporting tag.
135	- **One-click unsubscribe** per **RFC 8058** (`List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post`), processed **within 2 days**.
136	- **Spam complaint rate < 0.3%** (hard ceiling) via **Google Postmaster Tools**; operational target **< 0.1%**.
137	- Valid forward + reverse DNS (FCrDNS) and TLS on transmission.
138	- **Escalation:** Feb 2024 = temp deferrals (421-4.7.26/.30/.32); **Nov 2025 Gmail escalated to permanent rejection (550-5.7.26)** for unauthenticated mail. Full enforcement across providers in 2026. ([redsift 2026 checklist](https://redsift.com/guides/bulk-email-sender-requirements), [mailgun yahoogle](https://www.mailgun.com/state-of-email-deliverability/chapter/yahoogle-bulk-senders/), [autospf two years on](https://autospf.com/blog/google-yahoo-bulk-sender-mandate-changes-over-two-years/))
139	
140	**Microsoft / Outlook (enforced May 5 2025), for 5,000+/day to Outlook.com/Hotmail.com/Live.com:**
141	- **SPF + DKIM + DMARC** all required; DMARC min **p=none**, aligned to SPF or DKIM (ideally both).
142	- Non-compliant mail was first **junked**, moving toward **rejection**; treat SPF+DKIM+DMARC as mandatory to reach Outlook consumer inboxes. Microsoft doesn't publish the 0.3% number but the same hygiene applies. ([microsoft tech community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftdefenderforoffice365blog/strengthening-email-ecosystem-outlook%E2%80%99s-new-requirements-for-high%E2%80%90volume-senders/4399730), [mailgun MS requirements](https://www.mailgun.com/blog/deliverability/microsoft-sender-requirements/), [validity MS rules](https://www.validity.com/blog/keeping-the-inbox-safe-microsofts-new-bulk-email-rules-explained/))
143	
144	> **Cold-email caveat:** the 5,000/day thresholds are *per-provider consumer volume*. A rotation setup sending 20–40/inbox stays under it per inbox — but **compliance is not optional even below 5k**: sub-threshold senders that fail auth or spike complaints still get filtered, and the auth requirements are now the de-facto floor for *any* sender. Build to the strict standard regardless of volume.

146	**Legislation (status + 2025–2026 changes):**
147	- **CAN-SPAM (US):** permissive — cold email allowed without prior consent, but requires accurate From/subject, a functional opt-out honored promptly, and a **valid physical postal address** (commonly missed). Penalty raised to **up to $53,088 per email, effective Jan 17 2025**. ([instantly compliance](https://instantly.ai/blog/b2b-email-list-compliance-gdpr-canspam/), [growleads is cold email legal 2026](https://growleads.io/blog/is-cold-email-legal-gdpr-can-spam-2026/))
148	- **GDPR (EU/UK):** B2B cold email allowed under **legitimate interest** (no explicit consent) *only* with a documented Legitimate Interest Assessment, business (not personal) addresses, role-relevant messaging, disclosure of data source, and easy opt-out. Fines up to **€20M / 4% global revenue**. **New:** France's **CNIL rules effective Aug 2026 require explicit opt-in for all B2C prospecting** (email/phone/SMS) — watch for other member states following. ([outreachbloom compliance 2026](https://outreachbloom.com/cold-email-compliance), [inboxkit compliance](https://www.inboxkit.com/learn/cold-email-compliance-gdpr-can-spam))
149	- **CASL (Canada):** strictest — **consent required before the first send** (express or implied via an existing business relationship in the last 2 years). Fines up to **$10M CAD/violation (orgs), $1M CAD (individuals)**. ([moderninbound compliance](https://moderninbound.com/blog/cold-email-compliance-guide))
150	- **2026 trend:** regulators are actively cracking down on unsolicited commercial email and **AI-generated outreach is accelerating enforcement / creating new exposure**. Suppression, consent records, and jurisdiction handling must be first-class, not bolted on.
151	
152	**Mandatory-NOW checklist to reach the inbox:** ① SPF + DKIM (aligned) on every sending domain · ② DMARC published (min p=none, RUA) · ③ RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe on marketing mail, honored ≤2 days · ④ complaint rate <0.3% (target <0.1%) monitored via Postmaster · ⑤ dedicated cold domain + subdomain, warmed · ⑥ verified list (bounce <3%) · ⑦ physical address + honest identification + working opt-out (CAN-SPAM) · ⑧ documented lawful basis per recipient jurisdiction (GDPR/CASL).

192	
193	- **Campaign view:** delivery, bounce (hard/soft split), reply + **positive-reply** (hero metric), click, complaint, unsubscribe, inbox-placement. Time series + funnel.
194	- **Open rate: show it, but flag it.** Render behind an "⚠ inflated by Apple MPP / scanners — not a reliable signal" tooltip, visually de-emphasized, never the headline and never an optimization target. This honesty is a differentiator vs tools that still lead with opens.

199	## D. Multi-domain / multi-inbox management + rotation + auto-pause
200	
201	- **Pool manager:** register domains → subdomains → inboxes; run and cache SPF/DKIM/DMARC/tracking verification; show a readiness matrix.
202	- **Rotation engine** in the send worker: distribute a campaign's daily sends round-robin across *eligible* inboxes (status=active, under `currentRampCap`, warmup complete, auth green), spacing sends `minGapSeconds` (90–120s) inside each inbox's send window; respect per-inbox and per-domain caps (20–40/inbox, ~100–250/domain). Persist last-used to avoid clustering.
203	- **Auto-pause on bad metrics (the safety system):** evaluate `HealthSnapshot` rules continuously —
204	  - bounce ≥1.8%/inbox/day → **pause inbox**; sustained >2% over multiple days → **pause domain**; >5% → **hard stop + require re-verification**.
205	  - complaint >0.08%/domain → **pause domain + flag targeting**.
206	  - On pause: stop new sends, keep the inbox warming, notify, and require manual/verified re-activation. Never silently keep burning a domain.
207	- **Deliverability inbox rescue:** on soft-bounce spikes, back off volume automatically (adaptive ramp down), don't just hard-pause.

210	
211	- **Auth-or-no-send:** worker refuses to send from any domain lacking passing SPF+DKIM+DMARC (min p=none). This is now table stakes (§5).

217	- **Verify-before-send:** integrate list verification (ZeroBounce/NeverBounce/Bouncer) as a pre-send step; block campaigns whose projected bounce (from verification) exceeds ~3%.

For the Suppression reason enum, the spec mentions distinguishing hard bounces but that's better handled at the event level, so I'll keep the enum as-is with UNSUBSCRIBE, BOUNCE, COMPLAINT, and MANUAL.

## Cold Email Engine — Phase 3 (deliverability + scale layer) (2026-08-11)

Phase 3 adds the **deliverability / scale** layer the 2026 research demands: multi-domain / multi-inbox
rotation, per-inbox **warming**, **honest** deliverability analytics, and **health-based auto-pause**. Built
on branch `feature/coldemail-phase3`. Additive to Phase 1/2 — no existing model or enum value changed, and
the master kill-switch `cold_email_sending_enabled` (default **false**) still gates every send.

**The 2026 framing (why this shape):** open rate is broken — Apple Mail Privacy Protection pre-loads
tracking pixels so 50%+ of "opens" are machine-generated. Inbox access is now gated by **authentication**
(SPF+DKIM+DMARC + RFC 8058 one-click unsub + complaint rate <0.3%), not content. So Phase 3 optimises on
**reply / positive-reply, bounce, complaint, click, unsubscribe, and inbox-placement** — never opens — and
on **health-monitored multi-inbox rotation with auto-pause**, because one burned domain poisons every
recipient on it.

### New data models (additive)
- **`SendingDomain`** — a dedicated cold-email domain owned by a `Brand` (reputation isolated off the primary
  brand domain). Fields: `domain`, `subdomain`, `isPrimary`, `status` (PENDING/WARMING/ACTIVE/PAUSED/BURNED),
  `spf/dkim/dmarcVerified`, `dmarcPolicy`, `trackingDomain` + `trackingDomainVerified`, `oneClickUnsub`,
  `reputationScore`, `warmupStartedAt`, `pausedReason`.
- **`Inbox`** — a mailbox on a `SendingDomain` (a domain has many). `provider` (GMAIL/M365/SMTP/POSTAL/KUMO),
  `status` (WARMING/ACTIVE/PAUSED/BURNING), `dailyCap`, `currentRampCap`, `warmupDay`, warmup plan
  (`strategy`, `warmupMode`, `startCap`, `targetCap`, `rampDays`), `sendWindowStart/End`, `minGapSeconds`,
  `healthScore`, `lastSendAt`.
- **`WarmupState`** — per-inbox, per-day planned-vs-actual ramp + warmup signals (replies, spam-rescues).
- **`DeliverabilityEvent`** — append-only analytics spine (SENT/DELIVERED/DEFERRED/HARD_BOUNCE/SOFT_BOUNCE/
  OPEN/CLICK/REPLY/POSITIVE_REPLY/COMPLAINT/UNSUBSCRIBE/PLACEMENT_TEST) with loose inbox/domain/campaign/
  contact/send ids. Everything else rolls up from it.
- **`PlacementTest`** — inbox-placement (seed) results (`inbox/spam/promotions/missing %`), the only
  trustworthy "in the inbox?" signal. Manual entry now; a GlockApps/MailReach API writes the same rows later.
- **`MetricsDaily`** — precomputed daily rollup per scope (CAMPAIGN/INBOX/DOMAIN/BRAND). Rates are DERIVED,
  not stored. `opens` retained but **UNRELIABLE**.
- **`HealthSnapshot`** — per-scope daily health score + status + `triggeredRules`, feeding auto-pause.
- Extended additively: `EmailEventType` (+REPLY, POSITIVE_REPLY, HARD_BOUNCE, SOFT_BOUNCE, DEFERRED),
  `ConsentBasis` (+EXISTING_RELATIONSHIP for CASL), `ConsentRecord.assessmentRef`, `ColdSend.inboxId`,
  `Brand.sendingDomains`.

### Pure, tested logic (no DB/IO)
- **`lib/coldemail/warmup.ts`** — ramp presets (Conservative 5→30/28d, Standard 5→40/21d, Aggressive
  10→50/14d, Adaptive), `warmupDailyLimit` (linear ramp), `inboxAllowedVolume` (ramp clamped by dailyCap +
  adaptive health back-off), `warmupRampCurve`, `warmupStatus`. `WARMUP_MODES` flags synthetic-pool warmup
  as **risky** (real-seed/hybrid preferred; a real shared warmup network is out of scope — SaaS-pool).
- **`lib/coldemail/rotation.ts`** — `selectNextInbox` (least-recently-used, cap + auth + min-gap gated),
  `planRotation`, and the **auto-pause thresholds** from research §4: inbox pause **1.8%** bounce, domain
  pause **2%** bounce, hard-stop **5%**, domain complaint pause **0.08%** — all Settings-tunable.
- **`lib/coldemail/analytics.ts`** — `deriveRates` (delivery/bounce/complaint/click/reply/positive-reply/
  unsub over the correct denominators), benchmark bands, composite `healthScore` that **excludes opens by
  construction**, and `OPEN_RATE_WARNING`.

### Worker
- `worker/coldemail.ts` — the send sweep now **rotates** across a brand's ACTIVE inboxes (on non-paused,
  authenticated domains), sending AS each inbox address, honouring per-inbox warmup limit + dailyCap + min
  gap; writes `ColdSend.inboxId` + a `DeliverabilityEvent`. Falls back to the Phase 2 brand-cap path when a
  brand has no inboxes.
- `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts` — **warmup sweep** (recompute ramp caps + WarmupState, promote warmed
  authenticated inboxes to ACTIVE) and **rollup+auto-pause sweep** (DeliverabilityEvent → MetricsDaily +
  HealthSnapshot; pause burning inboxes/domains). Both are send-independent and run regardless of the
  kill-switch (they maintain state, never send). Registered in `worker/index.ts`.

### Admin UI (under the "Cold Email" entry)
- **Domains & inboxes** (`/admin/coldemail/domains`) — register domains → inboxes, a per-domain **readiness
  panel** for the 2026 bulk-sender rules (aligned SPF+DKIM+DMARC, RFC 8058 one-click unsub, custom tracking
  domain) with red/green + guidance link, and auth/DMARC-policy toggles.
- **Warming** (`/admin/coldemail/warming`) — per-inbox ramp curve, day/target, health, plain-language status,
  and a prominent warning that synthetic-pool warmup can hurt in 2026.
- **Analytics** (`/admin/coldemail/analytics`) — overview trends + per-domain and per-inbox health tables.
  **Open rate is shown but flagged** "unreliable (MPP-inflated) — do not optimize on this"; reply/positive-
  reply/bounce/complaint/click/placement are the primary signals. Manual **seed-test** + **deliverability
  signal** recorders (no external API).
- Server actions in `lib/actions-coldemail.ts` (each re-checks `requireArea("platform")`): domains, inboxes,
  warmup start, seed results, manual signals; Settings extended with the burn thresholds.
